title: Ed Case highlights community events and legislative efforts in recent social media posts - East Houston News
text:
U.S. Representative Ed Case, who has represented Hawaii’s 1st district in Congress since 2019, recently posted a series of updates on his official X (formerly Twitter) account. The posts cover local community events, environmental policy concerns, and legislative initiatives.
On December 1, 2025, Case shared his participation in Honolulu’s annual holiday celebration: “Before redeyeing back to a cold DC December, I joined Mayor Blangiardi, his great City team and so many others at Honolulu Hale at the festive kickoff of Honolulu City Lights 2025 and lighting of the City Holiday Tree, all inspired by this year’s theme, “Navigating by the https://t.co/iaWWefJTfq”.
The following day, December 2, Case addressed environmental issues stemming from federal policy changes: “Among the most disturbing of the Trump administration’s multi-front attack on decades of environmental protections: the Environmental Protection Agency’s rollback of hard-fought limits on PFAS “forever chemicals” in our drinking water. I joined @RepLaMonica and over 100 other https://t.co/Cxf9bVtfKg”.
On December 3, he announced support for housing affordability measures: “I joined my colleague @RepBeatty (Ohio) on her proposal to assist first-time homebuyers by reducing their mortgage payments on completion of a housing finances education program. More here: https://t.co/DSiVSLNqpI. https://t.co/66OMpQqdqF”.
Case has served as U.S. Representative for Hawaii’s 1st District since replacing Colleen Hanabusa in 2019 and previously served in the Hawaii House of Representatives from 1994 to 2002. Born in Hilo in 1952 and currently residing in Kāneʻohe, Case holds degrees from Williams College and UC Hastings Law School.
